chunks: Ishaq ibn Ammar narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام that he said:
"One who consumes carrion, blood, or pork is subject to disciplinary punishment; if he returns to it, he is disciplined."
I said, "And if he returns again?" He said: "He is disciplined, and there is no execution upon him."

key_terms.آكِلُ الْمَيْتَةِ: one who eats carrion, meaning an animal not slaughtered according to the law
key_terms.أَدَبٌ: disciplinary punishment or correction imposed by authority
key_terms.لَحْمِ الْخِنْزِيرِ: pork, the flesh of swine, which is forbidden

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for repeatedly eating carrion, blood, or pork in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who consumes carrion, blood, or pork. The punishment stated is disciplinary punishment (ta'dib), and even with repeated offense, the ruling remains discipline rather than execution.
